profile_headline: Founder, ConceptOwl. Ex-IPS. Teaching science to rural India.
post_content:
A few years ago, we were running around like headless chickens looking for
vendors for data entry of science/math questions into our software platform
using LaTeX. We settled on a vendor in Chennai after going through a nightmare
with four other vendors. But things were still a mess. One day I got fed up
and spent 4-5 hrs on a Sunday learning how to use LaTeX and some
idiosyncrasies of our system. The next day we trained our team and within 2-3
days, the process was running smoothly in our office. It is amazing how much
easier it is to learn something than to run away from it. Yet, we did that for
almost one year. Similarly, our mobile app was once too slow and a developer
with 10+ years experience was not able to fix it. I asked a colleague, who had
done just a little Java programming a decade ago, to learn Ruby on Rails from
scratch and fix the platform. In 8 months, she fixed the problems which
experienced folks could not. Even today, those fixes are in place. Over the
years, I have learned that all you need is an intelligent person with a
ferocious drive and thirst for learning. Sans that, experience, degrees, and
pedigree are all garbage. And if you are in a leadership position, you better
be that person. Else get out of the way for someone more deserving.
